a.summary: Main commit 91bc814 added a bounds guard to this method in TransactionRecord; the version hoisted into BaseTransaction by v1_tx has no guard at all. Without it `signatureOffset(index)` is computed from an unvalidated index: for legacy/v0 `1 + (Integer.MIN_VALUE * 64)` wraps to exactly 1, i.e. an invalid negative index silently overwrites the fee payer's signature slot; other out-of-range indexes either write into the message body or throw ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException after the signer has already been invoked. Main's test `TransactionSigningTests.signIndexRejectsSlotsOutsideTheRequiredSignerRegion` pins both the `Integer.MIN_VALUE` case and `index == numSigners()`, and additionally asserts the signer is never invoked (`signer.signInvocations() == 0`), which requires the guard to run before any offset arithmetic.

b.summary: VERIFIED (find-string confirmed unique). Main commit 91bc814 added a bounds guard to this method in TransactionRecord; the version hoisted into BaseTransaction has none, so `signatureOffset(index)` is computed from an unvalidated index. For legacy/v0 `1 + (Integer.MIN_VALUE * 64)` wraps to exactly 1 (checked: -2^31 * 2^6 ≡ 0 mod 2^32), i.e. an invalid negative index silently overwrites the fee payer's signature slot; other out-of-range indexes write into the message body or throw ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException only after the signer has already been invoked. Main's `TransactionSigningTests.signIndexRejectsSlotsOutsideTheRequiredSignerRegion` pins both `Integer.MIN_VALUE` and `index == numSigners()` with `assertThrowsExactly(IllegalArgumentException.class, ...)`, asserts the serialized bytes are unchanged, and asserts `signer.signInvocations() == 0`, which requires the guard to run before any offset arithmetic. Main's Javadoc added in 0d68f02 to `Transaction.sign(int, Signer)` documents exactly this contract ("@throws IllegalArgumentException if {@code index} is negative or is not less than {@link #numSigners()}"), so without this fix the merged interface documentation would be a lie. The guard generalizes correctly to V1Transaction, whose `numSigners()` reads the build-time header byte data[1].
